relevance_note: Case report of a Latvian family with two hemizygous males and two heterozygous carrier mothers with LAMP2 c.928+3A>G: "two male patients, hemizygous for a novel splice-affecting variant c.928+3A>G".
method_note: Hand extraction from text and Table 1 (columns: Patient | Variant Status | Cardiac Symptoms | Cognitive Impairment | Retinal Symptoms | Myopathic Symptoms); Table 1 'None' cells are words, not symbols; 'N/A' cells treated as not reported. Labels: 'Patient 1'/'Patient 2' (paper's labels; pedigree II-3/III-1), mothers labelled by pedigree labels I-2 and II-2. is_proband left null for the patients: the figure legend says index patients are denoted with arrows but the text does not say which. II-2 is not stated in the text to be I-2's daughter, so no inheritance recorded for either mother. Functional (RNA splicing) evidence, pathogenicity and ACMG PS3 recorded only for the two patients, whose RNA was tested; mothers' RNA was not analysed. Authors' classification history: VUS at testing, VarSome likely pathogenic, authors propose pathogenic (recorded). Patient 1 CK 'at the upper limit of the reference range, 175–297 U/L (Ref < 190 U/L)' is ambiguous, so no feature row and elevated CK not reported. Patient 1 tigroid/cystic macular changes not mapped to the pigmentary retinopathy checklist item (left not reported). Preserved LVEF does not address dilation, so the composite 'dilated or hypokinetic LV' item left not reported. 'None of the mothers has a clinically diagnosed intellectual disorder' recorded as an excluded group-statement row for both mothers, but the broader checklist item left not reported (narrower absence; no formal testing; Table 1 N/A). Patient 2 HCM not mapped to LVH checklist item (LV hypertrophy not stated). Patient 2: unremarkable early motor development vs delayed psychomotor development both recorded (not a direct contradiction). Healthy/unaffected relatives used as RNA controls are not individually described and get no rows. Families from refs [12]-[14] and [25] in the Discussion are described only at family/group level and get no rows. No stacked cells. No contradictions found.

span: roughly 80% of the transcripts of the amplified region in the affected patients’ samples lacked all of exon 7 (64 bp in length), with the remaining 20% retaining the complete correct sequence
The loss of exon 7 would cause a shift in the open reading frame and introduce a premature stop codon downstream
No changes in transcripts, however, were observed in the samples from unaffected family members.
